correctness.rationale: The proof covers every integer n>=3 and 2<=k<=n-1 by a monotone inverse-image domination lemma on cyclic intervals, including the terminal-point boundary case. Initial singleton k is optimal, successive k-length B expansions and A rotations exhaust all cases of (n-1) mod k; their reversed word is an actual reset witness. The standard-library verifier cross-checks 105 exact forward subset-BFS instances, 53,130 inverse cyclic intervals and 1,606 large witnesses. Exhaustion for finite n alone is not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The natural nonidempotent successor-chain deformation of the Černý cyclic family is fully solved in two integer parameters, not a cherry-picked slice. A sharp reset threshold with explicit shortest words and a proved globally greedy inverse-interval mechanism identifies a quadratic-to-linear complexity crossover as the successor-chain length scales with n. Generic upper bounds and existence criteria cannot provide that exact classification; the specific invariant is the canonical reset threshold.
